items.title: Bill Charlap interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, April 16, 2000
items.q: It was a Verve two-fer that had a lot of “Night Train” on it, much of the classic trio with Ray Brown and Ed Thigpen. Those were real important.

ctx.x: Yeah. Definitely. Do you have a few precious recordings to you that really made an impression on you as you were growing up?

It changes all the time. Because there are so many recordings. I happen to have a very large library of recorded music which I’ve collected over the years, just out of being a fan. It’s quite large and pretty comprehensive. I listen to a great deal of classical music and jazz, and I can remember important records in many — not that many genres, but mostly classical music and jazz. I know the first record I bought was Vladimir Horowitz playing Liszt, the “Hungarian Rhapsody #2,” the one that he did live at…
Did your mother feel good about your career path into music?
